create.name: Dorje Chang Institute
create.bio:
Known in full as the Dorje Chang Institute for Wisdom Culture, this Tibetan Buddhist centre in Avondale, Auckland, calls itself the oldest centre of its kind in New Zealand. It became a registered charitable trust in 1976, so the end of 2026 marks fifty years of work in the city. The institute belongs to the FPMT, the international network begun by Lama Thubten Yeshe and Lama Zopa Rinpoche, and teaches in the Gelug lineage that comes down from Lama Tsongkhapa. Its resident teacher is Geshe Wangchen, and a resident nun coordinates the spiritual programme.

The centre sits in spacious grounds with a stupa, a large prayer wheel for world peace, outdoor Buddha statues, gardens and a fruit orchard, which it describes as a green oasis in the city. Its programme runs from introductory Sunday morning talks and the FPMT Discovering Buddhism and Buddhist Mind Science series, many led by long-time student Simon Harrison, to guided meditation evenings on Tuesdays and the five-year Basic Program for committed students. There are also pujas, a library, a bookshop and a volunteer garden team. Classes ask a small facility contribution, audio recordings can be requested by people who live too far away, and monthly Dharma Friend supporters attend regular teachings free.

courses.title: Dharma Friend Supporter
courses.description: Monthly supporter membership of the centre for individuals or families, with free entry to regular teachings, discounts on some courses, retreats and visiting teachers, library borrowing and shop discounts. A higher Vajra level adds a Tibetan calendar. A minimum of six months is asked.

courses.title: Sunday Morning Classes
courses.description: Introductory Dharma talks and classes on Sunday mornings from 10am to noon, open to everyone, with topics announced on the centre's programme calendar; audio recordings can be requested by those who cannot attend.
courses.price: Requested facility contribution $10 per regular class

free_resources.title: Experiencing the Benefit of Mantras
free_resources.description: A free guide to mantra recitation with pages for the Tara, Avalokiteshvara and Padmasambhava mantras, covering their meaning, pronunciation and visualisation, plus short and long ways to set a motivation and dedicate the practice, drawn from Lama Zopa Rinpoche's advice.
